sources.entry: Imark - Open-source Markdown reader that stores your comments inside the document itself as HTML comments. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/migsilva89/imark) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]
Imark - Markdown reader that keeps your comments inside the .md file, with a Quick Look extension, live reload, and a skill that lets coding agents open a document for review and wait for your notes.

summary.one_liner: Native macOS Markdown reader that renders .md files and stores your comments inside the document as HTML comments.
summary.what_it_does: Imark is a native macOS app that opens .md files rendered, reloads them when they change on disk, and previews them in Finder via Quick Look. You can select text and attach a comment; the comment is written into the .md file as an HTML comment with a quote= attribute, so it stays with the document and is invisible in GitHub-style renderers. A toggle switches the view to a plain text editor with line numbers, a change gutter, and ⌘S to save, while saves and comments refuse to write if the file changed on disk since it was read. It renders GitHub-flavoured Markdown including tables, task lists, footnotes, front matter, Mermaid diagrams and KaTeX maths, with a foldable heading outline, wiki-link navigation and tabs. It can also be used from a terminal via an imark command, and it includes a skill and Claude Code plugin so coding agents can open a document for review and wait for Approve or Send Back.
use_cases: read markdown files on a mac
review a markdown plan or document from a coding agent
leave comments in a markdown file
preview md files with the space bar in Finder
export markdown comments as a blockquote for GitHub review
edit a markdown file with live reload and save
view markdown with diagrams and math
how_to_run: Or download the latest release and drag Imark.app into /Applications
cd renderer && npm ci && cd ..  (building from source)
notable: Comments are stored inside the .md file as HTML comments, so they travel with the document and are invisible in other renderers
Quick Look extension renders the document itself, not raw text
Coding agents can open a document for review and read notes back through a file in ~/.imark/pending, with no server
Editing mode refuses to save if the file changed on disk since it was read
No external Swift dependencies; bundled JavaScript rendering works offline
caveats: Built and maintained by one person; no support promise or release schedule
Quick Look extension requires the network client entitlement, though it does not use the network
